chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abu Abdullah al-Barqi, raising it (to the Prophet), said:
When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) married Fatima (peace be upon her), they said, 'With harmony and sons.' He said, 'No, but say, 'Upon goodness and blessings.'

key_terms.الرِّفَاءِ: Harmony, comfort, or ease in marital life

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say when people wished for harmony and sons for Fatima?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Prophet’s preference for spiritual and comprehensive well-being (*al-khayr wa al-baraka*) over specific worldly attributes like harmony or progeny, reflecting the Shia emphasis on divine blessing as the ultimate measure of success. Scholars note that this correction underscores the importance of seeking Allah’s general mercy and goodness in all matters, rather than limiting supplications to material or familial outcomes. The narration serves as a model for Islamic etiquette in congratulation, prioritizing eternal value over transient desires.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Abu Abdullah Al Barqy, raising it, said,

‘When Rasool-Allah<sup>asws</sup> got Fatima<sup>asws</sup> to be married, they (people) said, ‘(May she<sup>asws</sup> be) with the harmony and the sons’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But (say), ‘Upon the goodness and the Blessings’.
en.sarwar: 52. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from abu ‘Abd Allah, al-Barqiy in a marfu’ manner has said the following:

“When the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, gave Fatimah, Alayha al-Salam, in marriage and people said, ‘We wish her prosperity and sons, but he (the Messenger of Allah) said, ‘No, we wish for her goodness and blessings.’”
